question: True or false: as the dying Sun swells into a red giant, Earth's orbit will grow wider?
answer: True. The swelling Sun blows away about a third of its mass as wind, so its grip weakens and every planet drifts outwards; Earth's orbit could widen by about half. It may not be enough. Schröder and Smith calculated that tides raised on the bloated Sun would still drag Earth inwards to be swallowed.
move: When the centre loses weight, whatever circles it drifts away.
trap: Picturing the Sun that swallows Earth as pulling planets closer.
reference: Schröder & Smith, Distant future of the Sun and Earth revisited, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 386, 155, 2008
